Indian Standard INDUSTRIAL TEXTILES -- COTTON BACKING CLOTH FOR ABRASIVES -- SPECIFICATION ('First Revision)
1 SCOPE This standard prescribes the requirements of cotton backing cloth used as backing material in the manufacture of coated abrasives. 2 REFERENCES The standards given below contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility ot applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below: IL7 No. 199:1989
Ti[le

[S No. 3919:1966

Title Methods for sampling fabrics for determination characteristics of cotton of physical

5463:1969

Methods for sampling of cotton fabrics for chemical tests

3 MANUFACTURE 3.1 Yarn The cotton yarn used in the manufacture of cotton backing cloth shall be satisfactory in evenness and reasonably free from neps, knots, lumps, spinning and doubling defects. 3.2 Cloth The cloth shall be evenly and firmly woven in twill weave and shall be reasonably free from foreign matter and defects, such as missing ends, missing picks, floating ends, float ing picks and irregularities of twist in yarn. 3.3 The cloth shall be dyed with suitable dyes to shades as agreed to between the buyer and the seller. 4 REQUIREMENTS 4.1 The cotton backing cloth shall conform to the requirements given in Table I except for count of yarn which is given for gr,!idance only. 4.2 The length and width of cotton backing cloth shall be as agreed to bet~ een the buyer and the seller subject to the tolerance in IS 1954. 5 PACKING The cotton backing cloth for abrasives shall be packed in accordance with the procedure laid down in either IS 1347 or IS 293 as required. 6 MARKING 6.1 Each package of cloth shall be marked with the following: a) Name of the manufacturer, b) Name of the material; c) Net mass, in kg; 1 initials or trade-mark; +I crcent and +1 percent -0,5 p respect ively when dtterm ined by the method prescribed of -
